name: Half Speed
description: Plays what you are playing at half speed as you play it: an octave down and twice as slow, in repeating cycles that can chop like a rhythm or run together into one slow, deep bed.

params.name: Power
params.description: Off passes the dry signal. Switching it fades over a moment, and switching On starts a new cycle from the note being played.

params.name: Length
params.description: How long each cycle lasts before the slowed sound jumps forward to catch up with your playing. Short cycles stutter; long ones drag whole phrases out behind you.

params.name: Speed
params.description: How slow the playback runs, and so how far the pitch drops: a fourth, a fifth, one octave or two. A change bends the pitch like a tape machine changing speed.

params.name: Fade
params.description: How much of each cycle is spent fading from the old cycle into the new one. Low is a tight cut, high lets the end of one cycle wash over the start of the next.

params.name: Smooth
params.description: At zero each cycle is heard to start, a rhythm of slowed chunks. Turned up, a second playback half a cycle behind fills the jumps until the sound runs on unbroken.

params.name: Jitter
params.description: Makes every cycle a little longer or shorter than the last, so the jumps stop ticking like a machine.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Removes lows from the slowed sound, which keeps a thick source from turning to mud an octave down.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Removes highs from the slowed sound, for a darker bed that sits under the dry signal.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Brings a second playback into the right side whose cycles run later than the left's. The further it is turned, the wider the slowed sound. The bass stays in the middle.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the slowed sound.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A live varispeed player in outline: read heads on a delay line that run slower than the input and start again from the present every cycle, with two heads half a cycle apart under windows that sum to one when Smooth is up (a delay-line pitch shifter with a window as long as the cycle). Not a model of any product. Each new head is placed where its waveform lines up with the heads already playing, after the approach of Verhelst and Roelands, 'An overlap-add technique based on waveform similarity (WSOLA) for high quality time-scale modification of speech', and the cross-fades make up their level by how alike the two sounds are, after the approach of Fink, Holters and Zölzer, 'Signal-matched power-complementary cross-fading and dry-wet mixing'. Both are followed in outline only; no constants or details come from either.
